patch.summary:
Thesis: General-purpose vs specialist — RingCentral documents a broader use-case set; Grasshopper is narrower/specialist.

General-purpose vs specialist. Choose Grasshopper only if your buying job matches “SMB virtual business numbers with extensions and apps — True Solo from $14/month annual (f” rather than RingCentral's shape. Choose RingCentral only if your buying job matches “Enterprise-grade UCaaS / cloud phone platform (RingEX) with deep call routing, video, team” rather than Grasshopper's shape. Workflow advantage: Grasshopper leans shared coverage; RingCentral leans sales-calling, contact-center. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: General-purpose vs specialist — RingCentral documents a broader use-case set; Grasshopper is narrower/specialist.
- Positioning: Grasshopper is SMB virtual business numbers with extensions and apps — True Solo from $14/month annual (flat account, not per seat).; RingCentral is Enterprise-grade UCaaS / cloud phone platform (RingEX) with deep call routing, video, team messaging and contact-centre options — Core from .
- Company-size focus: Grasshopper (solo, small-business) vs RingCentral (small-business, mid-market, enterprise).
- Workflow coverage skew: Grasshopper-leaning — vs RingCentral-leaning sales-calling, contact-center, team-communication.
- Researched limits: Grasshopper — Virtual-number / simple phone product — not full UCaaS (no native team chat or video meetings suite); RingCentral — Published seat floors are medium confidence — RingCentral often gates exact dollars behind quote/selector flows.

Limitations — Grasshopper: Virtual-number / simple phone product — not full UCaaS (no native team chat or video meetings suite); IVR, recording and simultaneous ringing require Solo Plus or above; RingCentral: Published seat floors are medium confidence — RingCentral often gates exact dollars behind quote/selector flows; Call recording and deeper CRM/CTI require Advanced or above.

Poor-fit cases: Grasshopper is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Virtual-number / simple phone product — not full UCaaS (no native team chat or video meetings suite) · RingCentral is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Published seat floors are medium confidence — RingCentral often gates exact dollars behind quote/selector flows · Avoid Grasshopper if you actually need RingCentral's motion (Enterprise-grade UCaaS / cloud phone platform (RingEX) with deep call routing, v)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
